hypotheses.text: Elevated body-fluid glycine concentration (hyperglycinemia) is a 100% sensitive biochemical discriminator of NFU1-associated spastic paraplegia (SPG93) from common classical hereditary spastic paraplegias (SPG4, SPG7, SPG11).
hypotheses.rationale: Because NFU1 is essential for lipoic acid biosynthesis and the function of the lipoylated H-protein subunit of the glycine cleavage system, defective NFU1 disrupts glycine catabolism. Classical HSPs do not involve lipoate synthesis or glycine cleavage, making hyperglycinemia a potentially absolute biochemical discriminator.

evidence.text: The adult-onset, slowly evolving NFU1 spastic paraplegia patient exhibited persistent high glycine concentration in the context of leukoencephalopathy.

source.title: New spastic paraplegia phenotype associated to mutation of NFU1
source.quote: Our case clearly suggests the importance of considering NFU1 mutation in slowly evolving leukoencephalopathy with high glycine concentration.

evidence.text: A patient presenting with spastic paraparesis due to homozygous NFU1 mutation (p.Gly189Arg) was found to have hyperglycinemia alongside cavitating white matter lesions.

source.title: A genetic mimic of cerebral palsy: Homozygous NFU1 mutation with marked intrafamilial phenotypic variation
source.quote: Hyperglycinemia and cavitating leukodystrophy are suggestive of an NFU1 mutation diagnosis.

evidence.text: Defects in Fe-S cluster biogenesis proteins including NFU1 impair lipoic acid cofactor production needed for the glycine cleavage system, yielding elevated glycine in body fluids.

source.title: Differential diagnosis of lipoic acid synthesis defects
source.quote: Lipoic acid (LA) is an essential cofactor required for the activity of five multienzymatic complexes... and the glycine cleavage system (GCS).

hypotheses.text: Cavitating leukodystrophy on neuroimaging is a variable age- and severity-dependent sign rather than an obligate feature of SPG93, being prominent in infantile/relapsing cases but subtle or absent in late-onset slowly progressive spastic paraplegia.
hypotheses.rationale: While cavitating leukoencephalopathy is pathognomonic of classic lethal infantile MMDS1 and seen in early-onset spastic variants, adult-onset SPG93 presentations frequently show only non-cavitating periventricular T2/FLAIR hyperintensities, which could lead to missed diagnoses if cavitation is treated as mandatory.

evidence.text: A 27-month-old girl presenting with spastic paraparesis had frontal white matter hyperintensity with evidence of partial cystic degeneration and cavitation.

source.title: A genetic mimic of cerebral palsy: Homozygous NFU1 mutation with marked intrafamilial phenotypic variation
source.quote: There was also evidence of partial cystic degeneration and cavitation in the frontal regions.

evidence.text: The milder, adult-onset NFU1 patient showed early non-cavitating white matter abnormalities combined with slowly progressive spastic paraparesis, cognitive impairment, and axonal neuropathy.

source.title: New spastic paraplegia phenotype associated to mutation of NFU1
source.quote: The early white matter abnormalities observed on MRI was combined with a mixed sensory-motor neuropathy in the third decade.

evidence.text: Classic severe NFU1 mutations lead to fulminant cavitating leukoencephalopathy, early-onset lethal impairment, and high glycine/lactate.

source.title: Cavitating leukoencephalopathy with multiple mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome and NFU1 mutations
source.quote: associated with defects in NFU1, represented by severe early onset neurological impairment, multiple defects of respiratory chain and PDHc, high lactate and glycine levels.

hypotheses.text: Elevated glycine and spinal/white-matter MRI lesions cannot differentiate SPG93 from other mitochondrial Fe-S cluster lipoylation defects (such as GLRX5 or BOLA3 deficiency), requiring targeted molecular sequencing for definitive separation.
hypotheses.rationale: Other genes involved in mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster maturation and lipoic acid cofactor transfer (notably GLRX5, BOLA3, and IBA57) cause variant non-ketotic hyperglycinemia with overlapping spastic paraparesis, axonal neuropathy, and leukoencephalopathy or spinal cord signal changes.

evidence.text: Patients with GLRX5 bi-allelic mutations present with complex spastic paraparesis, axonal neuropathy, non-ketotic hyperglycinemia, and MRI white matter or upper cervical spinal cord signal changes.

source.title: GLRX5-associated [Fe-S] cluster biogenesis disorder: further characterisation of the neurological phenotype and long-term outcome
source.quote: All had non-ketotic hyperglycinemia and a homozygous pathogenic c.151_153delAAG (p.K51del) change in GLRX5.

evidence.text: Defects in genes across the lipoic acid and Fe-S cluster biogenesis cascade (NFU1, BOLA3, IBA57, GLRX5, LIPT1) share a convergent biochemical signature of impaired glycine cleavage and pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency.

source.title: Differential diagnosis of lipoic acid synthesis defects
source.quote: In recent years, disease-causing mutations in genes encoding for proteins involved in LA metabolism have been reported: NFU1, BOLA3, IBA57, LIAS, GLRX5, LIPT1, ISCA2, and LIPT2.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact sensitivity and specificity of CSF versus plasma glycine elevation across all published NFU1/SPG93 patients compared to SPG11 and other complex HSPs?
new_directions.rationale: Establishing whether plasma glycine alone is reliably elevated or whether CSF glycine/glycine ratio is required will determine whether a routine peripheral blood test can screen out classical HSP mimics.

new_directions.question_text: How do spinal cord MRI abnormalities (e.g., dorsal column or cervical cord T2 hyperintensity) differ between NFU1/SPG93, GLRX5 deficiency, and canonical complex HSPs?
new_directions.rationale: While brain white matter lesions can fluctuate or resolve, spinal cord signal alterations may provide a distinct anatomical radiological hallmark separating Fe-S cluster defects from SPG4/7/11.
